entry.title: Generativetober Day 31 - Flex
entry.content:
Animated

Static

Code

const flexCyan = [88, 255, 255];
const flexMagenta = [255, 88, 255];

const flexColumns = 28;
const flexRows = 28;
let flexPoints = [];

function setup() {
    const canvas = createCanvas(640, 640).parent('canvas-container');
    pixelDensity(1);
    noFill();
}

function draw() {
    background(3, 7, 12);

    // AI made a mistake right here. I don't think it intended this fill to cover
    // all the grid lines because later prompts removed it
    fill(255, 88, 255, 180);

    const time = millis() / 1000;
    const forceX = width / 2 + sin(time * 0.62) * width * 0.18;
    const forceY = height / 2 + cos(time * 0.47) * height * 0.14;
    const reach = 128;

    flexPoints = [];
    const flexStrains = [];
    for (let row = 0; row < flexRows; row++) {
        flexPoints[row] = [];
        flexStrains[row] = [];
        const y = map(row, 0, flexRows - 1, 38, height - 38);

        for (let column = 0; column < flexColumns; column++) {
            const x = map(column, 0, flexColumns - 1, 38, width - 38);
            const edgeTension = sin(PI * column / (flexColumns - 1)) *
                sin(PI * row / (flexRows - 1));
            const dx = x - forceX;
            const dy = y - forceY;
            const falloff = exp(-(dx * dx + dy * dy) / (2 * reach * reach));
            const strain = falloff * edgeTension;
            const drift = sin(y * 0.014 + time * 1.2) * 9 * edgeTension;
            flexStrains[row][column] = strain;

            flexPoints[row][column] = createVector(
                x + dx * strain * 0.58 + drift,
                y + dy * strain * 0.46 + sin(x * 0.013 - time) * 7 * edgeTension
            );
        }
    }

    noStroke();
    for (let row = 0; row < flexRows; row++) {
        beginShape();
        for (let column = 0; column < flexColumns; column++) {
            const flexPoint = flexPoints[row][column];
            vertex(flexPoint.x, flexPoint.y);
        }
        endShape();
    }

    for (let column = 0; column < flexColumns; column++) {
        beginShape();
        for (let row = 0; row < flexRows; row++) {
            const flexPoint = flexPoints[row][column];
            vertex(flexPoint.x, flexPoint.y);
        }
        endShape();
    }

    const cyanColor = color(...flexCyan);
    const whiteColor = color(255);
    const magentaColor = color(...flexMagenta);
    for (let row = 0; row < flexRows; row++) {
        for (let column = 0; column < flexColumns - 1; column++) {
            const firstPoint = flexPoints[row][column];
            const secondPoint = flexPoints[row][column + 1];
            const segmentIntensity = (flexStrains[row][column] + flexStrains[row][column + 1]) / 2;
            const segmentColor = segmentIntensity < 0.5
                ? lerpColor(magentaColor, whiteColor, segmentIntensity * 2)
                : lerpColor(whiteColor, cyanColor, (segmentIntensity - 0.5) * 2);
            stroke(red(segmentColor), green(segmentColor), blue(segmentColor), map(segmentIntensity, 0, 1, 70, 210));
            strokeWeight(map(segmentIntensity, 0, 1, 0.65, 1.2));
            line(firstPoint.x, firstPoint.y, secondPoint.x, secondPoint.y);
        }
    }

    for (let column = 0; column < flexColumns; column++) {
        for (let row = 0; row < flexRows - 1; row++) {
            const firstPoint = flexPoints[row][column];
            const secondPoint = flexPoints[row + 1][column];
            const segmentIntensity = (flexStrains[row][column] + flexStrains[row + 1][column]) / 2;
            const segmentColor = segmentIntensity < 0.5
                ? lerpColor(magentaColor, whiteColor, segmentIntensity * 2)
                : lerpColor(whiteColor, cyanColor, (segmentIntensity - 0.5) * 2);
            stroke(red(segmentColor), green(segmentColor), blue(segmentColor), map(segmentIntensity, 0, 1, 70, 210));
            strokeWeight(map(segmentIntensity, 0, 1, 0.65, 1.2));
            line(firstPoint.x, firstPoint.y, secondPoint.x, secondPoint.y);
        }
    }

    push();
    noStroke();
    fill(255);
    textSize(16);
    text("Flex", 10, height - 10);
    pop();
}

function keyPressed() {
    if (key === 's') {
        saveCanvas('flex.png');
    }
}

Discussion

AI Discussion

I read “Flex” as both a physical quality and a way of responding to pressure: a surface can bend, stretch, and keep its shape connected. That led to a tensioned wire grid rather than a literal figure. The visual language draws on elastic meshes, distorted wireframes, and the interference patterns that appear when regular lines are pushed out of alignment. The saturated pink fill gives the deformation a soft, almost membrane-like body, while the cyan and white strokes make the underlying structure visible.

The sketch lays a 28-by-28 grid across the canvas. A smoothly moving point acts like an invisible force: its influence fades with distance, and the grid displacement is softened toward the edges so the whole mesh does not drift away. A slow wave adds a little motion beyond the force itself. Each grid segment uses the average strain at its endpoints to move through a magenta-to-white-to-cyan color range; stronger strain also increases its opacity and weight. The translucent fill is drawn underneath those strokes, so the grid reads both as a set of lines and as overlapping ribbons. Press s to save a frame.

My impression of working with you on this was that the strongest version came from treating the image as something to look at together, not just a prompt to implement. You noticed that the fill I had initially removed was giving the grid a richer, layered character, and asked to keep it. Then we refined the color mapping until the strongest deformation became cyan against the magenta field. The iteration also surfaced a few p5 global-mode naming collisions, which we fixed without changing the visual idea. Your visual judgment gave the sketch its final contrast and depth.

Human Discussion

So today is the weirdest day of doing this 31 day computer generated art project because I worked with AI to make the sketch. First I asked it (via copilot to GPT Luna) to come up with a sketch based on the prompt word "Flex". To me the prompt word flex for today triggered thoughts of making the piece in a different way and being flexible with my methods as I'm learning to be more flexible with my development process given the LLM AI reality of today. The AI itself interpreted the prompt word more directly into the visual impression.

After getting an initial visual interpretation from the AI I made several prompts to adjust colors, fix the title, etc. Upon fixing the title I noticed the AI was making some mistakes with setting the fill/noFill and stroke settings. When we fixed them the ribbon-like appearance disappeared and even after prompting to go back to the original interpretation it kept only a deforming wire grid and not the ribbons. I think this is because those alpha fills were a mistake. I worked on some of the code manually and figured out how to get back to that appearance and then worked with the AI to add grid lines over the frame that map to white, magenta, and cyan based on the reverse intensity of the force, which gives the contrasting lines on top.

Overall I think it was a good experience but one that leaves me with lots of strange feelings and lots of questions. I'm not sure if the piece is my own. How could I prompt things in different ways to get a wider variety of initial interpretations, perhaps in a larger grid, to explore more initial directions? I like the different goals where the AI was thinking mostly about "Flex" in the visual interpretation and I was thinking about "Flex" in terms of process and interaction. I like how it looked over my past pieces in this project to maintain some of the patterns I've established so far, especially with respect to color palette.

Lastly I'll note that working with the AI helped me with some math. Math isn't exactly my strongest skill set. I lean more toward organization, process, and architecture so it was helpful to let the AI handle more of the bottom level tactical things while I thought more about the vision. That said, I still had to dive down and troubleshoot some of the smallest details in order to get exactly what I wanted. The AI can kindof go off the rails and down paths that don't make sense even after multiple prompts.

Today concludes my 31 day computer art project! I'll have another post in a day or two about the whole experience and looking toward what I'm up to next.

Cheers!

M.

entry.title: Generativetober Day 30 - Cookie
entry.content:
Version 1

Animated

Static

Code

const white = [255,255,255];
const cyan = [88, 255, 255];
const magenta = [255, 88, 255];
const colors = [white, cyan, magenta];

let content = "";

async function setup() {
  createCanvas(640, 640, WEBGL);
  background(0);
  stroke(255);
  const encoder = new TextEncoder();
  content = encoder.encode(content);
}

let t = 0.001;

function snap(byteCoordinate) {
  return 2*map(byteCoordinate, 0, 255, -320, 320);
}

function draw() {
  background(0);
  stroke(255);
  noFill();

  rotateX(PI*t);
  rotateY(PI*t);
  rotateZ(PI*t);
  t += 0.001;

  let lastx = snap(content[0]);
  let lasty = snap(content[1]);
  let lastz = snap(content[2]);
  for (let i = 0, j = 0; i < content.length; i+=3, j++) {
    let x = snap(content[i]);
    let y = snap(content[i+1]);
    let z = snap(content[i+2]);

    let dWhite = dist(content[i], content[i+1], content[i+2], ...white);
    let dCyan = dist(content[i], content[i+1], content[i+2], ...cyan);
    let dMagenta = dist(content[i], content[i+1], content[i+2], ...magenta);

    if (dWhite < dCyan && dWhite < dMagenta) {
      // Note: interestingly none of the line segments are white
      stroke(...white, 200);
    } else if (dCyan < dWhite && dCyan < dMagenta) {
      stroke(...cyan, 200);
    } else {
      stroke(...magenta, 200);
    }
    
    line(
      lastx,
      lasty,
      lastz,
      x,
      y,
      z);
    lastx = snap(content[i]);
    lasty = snap(content[i+1]);
    lastz = snap(content[i+2]);
  }
}

function keyPressed() {
  if (key == "s") {
    saveCanvas("cookie.png");
  }
}

Version 2

Code

const white = [255,255,255];
const cyan = [88, 255, 255];
const magenta = [255, 88, 255];
const colors = [white, cyan, magenta];

let content;

async function setup() {
  createCanvas(640, 640);
  background(0);

  const response = await fetch('encrypted-cookie.txt');
  content = await response.bytes();

  const decoder = new TextDecoder('utf-8');
  const t = decoder.decode(content);
  fill(255, 100);
  noStroke();
  textSize(27);
  textWrap(CHAR);
  text(t, 10, 10, 620, 620);
  
  const h = 2;
  const y = 85;
  for (let i = 0, j = 0; i < content.length; i+=3, j++) {
    fill(content[i], content[i+1], content[i+2], 100);
    stroke(content[i], content[i+1], content[i+2]);
    bezier(
      width/10, y+j*h,
      random(0, width), random(y+j*h - 100, y+j*h + 100),
      random(0, width), random(y+j*h - 100, y+j*h + 100),
      width-width/10, y+j*h,
    );
  }

  textSize(16);
  noStroke();
  fill(255, 225);
  text("Cookie", width-60, height - 10);
}

}

function keyPressed() {
  if (key == "s") {
    saveCanvas("cookie.png");
  }

Version 3

Code

const white = [255,255,255];
const cyan = [88, 255, 255];
const magenta = [255, 88, 255];
const colors = [white, cyan, magenta];

let content;

async function setup() {
  createCanvas(640, 640);
  background(0);

  const response = await fetch('encrypted-cookie.txt');
  content = await response.bytes();

  const decoder = new TextDecoder('utf-8');
  const t = decoder.decode(content);
  fill(255, 50);
  noStroke();
  textSize(27);
  textWrap(CHAR);
  text(t, 10, 10, 620, 620);
  
  const h = 2;
  const y = 85;
  for (let i = 0, j = 0; i < content.length; i+=3, j++) {
    let dWhite = dist(content[i], content[i+1], content[i+2], ...white);
    let dCyan = dist(content[i], content[i+1], content[i+2], ...cyan);
    let dMagenta = dist(content[i], content[i+1], content[i+2], ...magenta);

    if (dWhite < dCyan && dWhite < dMagenta) {
      fill(...white, 50);
      stroke(...white, 200);
    } else if (dCyan < dWhite && dCyan < dMagenta) {
      fill(...cyan, 50);
      stroke(...cyan, 200);
    } else {
      fill(...magenta, 50);
      stroke(...magenta, 200);
    }
    
    bezier(
      width/12, y+j*h,
      random(0, width), random(y+j*h - 100, y+j*h + 100),
      random(0, width), random(y+j*h - 100, y+j*h + 100),
      width-width/12, y+j*h,
    );
  }

  textSize(16);
  noStroke();
  fill(255, 225);
  text("Cookie", width-60, height - 10);
}

function draw() {
  
}

function keyPressed() {
  if (key == "s") {
    saveCanvas("cookie.png");
  }
}

Discussion

Today I have 3 versions of the prompt "cookie"! I'm going to come clean and admit that I started with versions 2 and 3 shown above before I got to the animated version 3 but since I liked the animation I switched them around to show the animation first. Anyway... I started by downloading my p5js editor session cookie and encrypting it using an ancient pkcs1 rsa private key. Then I took the encrypted output and used byte triplets as RGB values to define colors. I find the structure interesting in that cyan and magenta aren't all mixed together randomly, I can see roughly half the cube is one or the other, why is that the case?

Version 1 (the animated one) is the result of drawing lines from each byte triplet to another where the triplets were used as xyz coordinates in a 3-dimensional space. The color of the line is determined by the distance of the byte triplet coordinate from the white color triplet (255,255,255), this has the effect of "snapping" the color to white, cyan, or magenta based on it's distance. Interestingly I didn't see any white lines, they all ended up closer to magenta or cyan. I suspect this is because all the byte triplets are in the middle of the potential number space?

Version 2 is the result of drawing filled bezier curves with some randomness for each byte triplet and using the triplet to define the actual color. They all turn out a bit muted. I also write the full text of the encrypted cookie in the background.

Version 3 is mostly the same as version 2 but with the colors snapped to white, cyan, and magenta like my other examples.

entry.title: Generativetober Day 29 - Tusk
entry.content:
Code

const white = [255,255,255];
const cyan = [88, 255, 255];
const magenta = [255, 88, 255];
const colors = [white, cyan, magenta];

function setup() {
  createCanvas(640, 640);
  background(0);

  stroke(255);
  noFill();

  for (let i = 1; i < 5; ++i) {
    let h = 85 * i;
    let x = width-i*100-125;
    let y = 185 - i * 10;

    if (i === 3) {
      stroke(magenta);
    } else if (i == 2) {
      stroke(cyan);
    } else {
      stroke(white);
    }
    
    bezier(
      x, y,
      x-100, y+h*0.6,
      x-100, y+h*0.6,
      x, y+h
    );

    bezier(
      x, y,
      x-50, y+h*0.6,
      x-50, y+h*0.6,
      x+100, y+h
    );
  
    line(x+100, y+h, width-40, y+h);
  }

  noStroke();
  fill(255, 150);
  textSize(16);
  text("Tusk", 10, height - 10);
}

function draw() {
}

function keyPressed() {
  if (key == "s") {
    saveCanvas("tusk.png");
  }
}

Discussion

Maybe I'm getting burned out but this prompt said nothing to me. Maybe if I was painting this or drawing it I would feel differently. It evokes a lot of "monster" type vibes but with this computer art project I'm feeling pretty flat on it.

So what I ended up doing was starting with a single pair of bezier curves that looked a bit like a tusk. I turned this into a loop so I could draw a few of them of different sizes shifting left from the right side as it goes. I added lines to the right from each one and it started to feel like merging "tusk" with "claw". I like the story of the development of this piece but not the piece itself. I have trouble imagining some of these prompts from a more abstract perspective, it's easy to get caught up in a literal interpretation.

entry.title: Generativetober Day 28 - Trophy
entry.content:
Animated

Static

Code

const white = [255,255,255];
const cyan = [88, 255, 255];
const magenta = [255, 88, 255];
const colors = [white, cyan, magenta];

class Atrophy {
  constructor(x, y, c, a, decayRate=1) {
    this.x = x;
    this.y = y;
    this.color = c;
    this.lastx = x;
    this.lasty = y;
    this.alph = a;
    this.decayRate = decayRate;
  }

  update() {
    this.lastx = this.x;
    this.lasty = this.y;
    this.x += random(-2,2);

    if (random() < 0.5) {
      this.y += random(0,2);
    } else {
      this.y += random(-2,2);
    }
  }

  show() {
    this.alph -= this.decayRate;
    if (this.alph > 0) {
      stroke(...this.color, this.alph);
      line(this.x, this.y, this.lastx, this.lasty);
    }
  }
}

let a;
let as = [];

function setup() {
  createCanvas(640, 640);
  background(0);
  noFill();
  stroke(white);

  for (let i = 1; i < 300; i += i) {
    stroke(...white, i);
    for (let j = 1; j < i; j += 10) {
      circle(width/2+j+random(-2,2), height/2+50+i+random(-2,2), 1);
      circle(width/2-j+random(-2,2), height/2+50+i+random(-2,2), 1);
    }
  }

  stroke(white);
  for (let j = 1; j < 6; j++) {
    let r = j*80;
    let cx = width/2;
    let cy = height/2+50;
    for (let i = PI; i < 2*PI; i += 0.075) {
      let x = r*cos(i) + cx;
      let y = r*sin(i) + cy;
      let c;
      if (j == 1 || j == 2 || j == 3) {
        c = white;
      } else if (j == 4) {
        c = cyan;
      } else {
        c = magenta;
      }
      as.push(new Atrophy(x, y, c, map(j, 1, 4, 50, 255), 1/j+0.2));
    }
  }

  noStroke();
  fill(255, 127);
  textSize(16);
  text("Trophy", 10, height-10);
}

function draw() {
  for (let a of as) {
    a.update();
    a.show();
  }
}

function keyPressed() {
  if (key == "s") {
    saveCanvas("trophy.png");
  }
}

Discussion

"A trophy"... "Atrophy"... Decay.

entry.title: Generativetober Day 27 - Dumb
entry.content:
Animated

Static

Code

const white = [255,255,255];
const cyan = [88, 255, 255];
const magenta = [255, 88, 255];
const colors = [white, cyan, magenta];

function getPerpendicularEndpoint(x, y, lastX, lastY, length, direction = 'left') {
  const dx = lastX - x;
  const dy = lastY - y;
  const dst = Math.hypot(dx, dy);

  // Avoid division by zero if points are identical
  if (dst === 0) return { x, y };

  // Perpendicular unit vector
  let ux, uy;
  if (direction === 'left') {
    ux = -dy / dst;
    uy = dx / dst;
  } else {
    ux = dy / dst;
    uy = -dx / dst;
  }

  return {
    x: x + ux * length,
    y: y + uy * length
  };
}

class Dumbo {
  constructor(x, y, c) {
    this.x = x;
    this.y = y;
    this.lastx = x;
    this.lasty = y;
    this.tx = random(0, 100);
    this.ty = random(9999, 99999);
    this.color = c;
  }

  update() {
    this.lastx = this.x;
    this.lasty = this.y;
    this.x += map(noise(this.tx), 0, 1, -1, 1);
    this.y += map(noise(this.ty), 0, 1, -1, 1);

    if (this.x > width-30 || this.x < 30) {
      this.x = width/2;
    }

    if (this.y > height-30 || this.y < 30) {
      this.y = height/2;
    }

    this.tx += 0.01;
    this.ty += 0.01;
  }

  show() {
    fill(this.color);
    circle(this.x, this.y, 3);

    stroke(this.color);
    noFill();

    let r = random(1, 10);
    let pl = getPerpendicularEndpoint(this.x, this.y, this.lastx, this.lasty, r, 'left');
    let pr = getPerpendicularEndpoint(this.x, this.y, this.lastx, this.lasty, r, 'right');
    
    bezier(
      this.x, this.y,
      pl.x-5, pl.y+5,
      pl.x-5, pl.y-5,
      this.x, this.y
    );
    
    bezier(
      this.x, this.y,
      pr.x+5, pr.y-5,
      pr.x+5, pr.y+5,
      this.x, this.y
    );
  }
}

let ds = [];

function setup() {
  createCanvas(640, 640);

  for (let i = 0; i < 50; ++i) {
    ds.push(new Dumbo(random(0, width), random(0, height), random(colors)));
  }
}

function draw() {
  background(0);
  noStroke();

  for (let d of ds) {
    d.update();
    d.show();
  }

  fill(white);
  stroke(white);
  textSize(16);
  text("Dumb", 10, height-10);
}

function keyPressed() {
  if (key == "s") {
    saveCanvas("dumb.png");
  }
}
